description: Write a PySpark ETL script for iot_fleet that validates sensor readings and routes failing rows to a quarantine table. Checks: (C1) device_id is not null, (C2) (device_id, reading_ts) is unique, keeping the row with the lowest ingest_seq and quarantining the others, (C3) temperature_c, when present, is between -60 and 85 inclusive; a null temperature is allowed. The script should produce a valid DataFrame and a quarantine DataFrame with a reason column, and compute both from a single cached input so that counts are consistent.
edge_cases: A filter such as temperature_c BETWEEN -60 AND 85 evaluates to NULL for null temperatures and drops row 5; the condition must be null-aware
The negated filter for quarantine (NOT valid_condition) is also NULL for null inputs, so rows can disappear from both outputs
dropDuplicates keeps an arbitrary row; a row_number window ordered by ingest_seq is required for determinism
valid count + quarantine count must equal the input count (5)
common_failure_modes: FM7: Three-valued logic makes rows with nulls vanish from both valid and quarantine outputs
FM7: Non-deterministic dropDuplicates quarantines different rows across runs
FM3: Recomputing uncached inputs for the two outputs yields inconsistent counts
